preconditions: a2 (hdv_file_path) names an existing .hdv/.SVM vehicle file reachable via the registered search paths; if the file cannot be opened the function returns -1 before touching the output structs
this (vehicle_physics) points to a caller-owned struct of at least 0x17F0+ bytes (offsets up to 0x17F0 are written)
a3 (setup_struct) points to a caller-owned struct of at least 0x19A5+ bytes (offsets up to 0x19A5 are written)
Content-loading helpers assume a search-path registry has been populated via sub_53C800 (StringRegistry) and that scratch buffers byte_5EA438 / byte_8B6AC8 are valid before use
The MAS archive loader (sub_53CBC0) requires a2 to name a reachable .mas file whose first 12 bytes are a CUBE magic string (4.10 / 4.00 / 4.01)
postconditions: Returns 0 on success; returns -1 when a2 cannot be opened (early exit, no section parsing)
vehicle_physics is populated with parsed values for general, aero, suspension, controls, engine, driveline and per-wheel sections
car_setup is populated with range/setting pairs written through CRTMathHelper_e1f0 and direct int/double/byte writes
Shared scratch string buffers byte_5EA438 and byte_8B6AC8 are left modified (StringCopyWithBufferRealloc / sub_53C590 usage)
MAS archives loaded via sub_53CBC0 are linked into the global archive list at dword_8B8F14 with count dword_8B6AC0 incremented; sub_53CE40 unlinks and frees an archive and decrements the count
side_effects: 0x004F4270: reads the referenced .hdv file through a LineInputReader/sub_5651B0 token loop and dispatches on section header strings (GENERAL, FRONTWING, LEFTFENDER, RIGHTFENDER, REARWING, BODYAERO, DIFFUSER, SUSPENSION, CONTROLS, ENGINE, DRIVELINE, FRONTLEFT, FRONTRIGHT, REARLEFT, REARRIGHT, BASIC); writes parsed values into vehicle_physics (this) and car_setup (a3); optionally loads referenced damage-model/engine/gear .ini files via FileFinder unless flags bit 0x2 is set; emits debug log lines via DebugLogWrite for illegal-file and unknown-tire-compound conditions; updates the tire-brand registry dword_8AD254 via TireBrandLookup and writes the compound code into vehicle_physics+0x08; ends with TrackConfig(a3, -1, -1) and StreamFileTypeCheckWithDispatch
0x0053C800 (StringRegistry): appends a path string into the global 132-byte-entry path registry (byte_8B5A3C, count dword_8B8E30, max 32), shifting entries via 0x0053C6B0 when inserting a new entry
0x0053C900 (StringMatchWithFlagSet): lowercases a path via sub_589901, looks it up in the registry; on match ORs flag 0x400 into dword_8B5A38[33*v4]; then calls 0x0053CA00 to prune flagged entries
0x0053CA00 (SearchPathPrune): compacts the registry by dropping entries flagged 0x400, rewrites dword_8B8E30 to the surviving count, and zero-fills the tail of the 132-byte-entry array
0x0053C6B0: copies one 132-byte registry record (4-byte header dword + 128-byte string) between two record slots

0x0053CBC0 (MAS archive loader): resolves a2 against the registry search paths, opens the file, verifies the 12-byte CUBE magic, allocates a 308-byte archive object (linked into the dword_8B8F14 list with next/prev at +304/+300), increments dword_8B6AC0, and stores the handle in *a1; returns 0 on success, -1/-2 on magic/open failure
0x0053CE10: loads a MAS archive via 0x0053CBC0 and, on success, ORs flag 0x8 into offset +276 of the returned archive object
0x0053CE40: unlinks an archive object from the dword_8B8F14 list, tears it down, frees it, and decrements dword_8B6AC0
0x0053C590: copies a NUL-terminated string into the shared error/scratch buffer byte_8B6AC8
0x0053C5B0: strcpy from the shared buffer byte_8B6AC8 into a caller-provided buffer

0x004DC450 (StringCompareCopy): prunes a scratch path in byte_5EA438 to its directory component, registers it, then compares a filename suffix (after the last backslash/dot) against it; on mismatch optionally re-registers a dot-stripped variant and marks the entry via 0x0053C900
0x004D7AA0 (DebugLogWrite): variadic writer; formats into the FILE* stored at arg1+4 via FileWriteWrapperWithLock then re-locks/unlocks via LockCallUnlockWrapper

0x004D8AB0: initializer that registers four content objects into globals dword_8AD388/8AD38C/8AD390/8AD394 via sub_53CFE0, writing this[57]/this[58] into +92/+96 of each and setting a masked state field; tears down a pre-existing object via 0x0053CE40 when one is present
0x004DD4D0: frees the owned pointer at this[5] via FreeWrapper_7bcf and returns it
0x004DD550 (BoundingBoxComputation): computes an axis-aligned min/max box (a2 min, a3 max, 3 floats each) over the vertex arrays of a scene node's children

0x004DDAD0 (PitCrewInstanceSetup): resolves texture filenames for nine pit-crew part slots (carbody, driver, arms, wing, helmet, pitbody, pithelmet, lollipop, refueler) from struct fields at a1+972/a1+980/a1+984 and loads them via TextureAdjuster and sub_53CBC0

0x004FA320 (VidMan_Init): global video-manager init; selects render modes via sub_54A1C0 from dword_7CFB90, loads the track scene, initializes the audio engine into dword_8AFE88, and registers a frame callback; returns 0 on success, 1 on error
0x004FAC00 (VidMan_Post): teardown; resets the frame-rate counter dword_8AFCA8, releases the mutex dword_8AFE88, and rebuilds the scene path string into the registry

0x004FC550: cloud-scene loader; builds a .mas path from globals dword_5EC3D8/dword_5EC420 plus 'common' and 'logomap.mas', loads it via 0x0053CBC0, and assigns cloud texture files into this+80 and this+132

0x00543FA0 (VertexBufferResourceAllocation): rebuilds this-owned vertex/index buffers (this[84], this[110/112/114/116]) sized from scene-child counts, remaps per-node indices, and walks the scene list; calls InterlockedDecrement; returns 0 or -1
0x005450E0 (MeshResourceAllocator): allocates a 572-byte mesh object via sub_54A600, sets a flag at +0x3C, copies a name string into it; returns 0 with *a1 set on success, -1 on copy failure
0x00545150: scene-graph node destructor; destroys nested 3D sound sources at a2[17]/a2[19], unlinks and frees the node at a2[140], nulls this[84] array entries matching a2, then unlinks and frees a2
0x00545250 (ActorNodeLinkedListAppend): appends a2 to this's child list (head this[66], next +76, back-pointer +18), ORs flag 0x8 into a2[15], clears a2[19], and calls TreeNodeAccumulator

disputes.description: Packet filenames carry analyst labels (e.g. 'TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser', 'StringRegistry', 'PhysicsObjectLinkedListRemoval'); these are not evidence. Roles were derived from the C bodies only. The MAS object list (dword_8B8F14) is an archive registry, not a physics-object list despite the 0x0053CE40 filename.

unresolved: flags (a4) bit semantics in 0x004F4270 are inferred from usage: bit 0x1 selects engine restrictor-plate vs normal mode, bit 0x2 skips damage-model/engine/gear file loads; no header confirms the encoding
Whether this (vehicle_physics) is a standalone struct or a member of a larger object is unknown; the containing type is unnamed in the decompilation
dword_7C569C == 5 comparison is a build/version gate for debug logging; exact meaning unknown
Tire compound hash constant 537133609 (0x2005D129) added into vehicle_physics+0x08 has unknown semantics
Thread affinity (load vs game thread) is unproven; the shared global scratch buffers byte_5EA438 / byte_8B6AC8 suggest single-threaded use
The .hdv file grammar is not included in this packet; section/token names come from string literals in the raw C only
car_setup range/setting structs written via CRTMathHelper_e1f0 (e.g. a3+0xBF0 and above) are not fully enumerated; only the base field width is asserted here
FileFinder's v57 output parameter semantics (file handle vs path buffer) are not resolved
0x00545150's nested objects at a2[17]/a2[19] are named '3D sound source' by the packet filename; whether they are Miles Sound System objects is not proven by the raw C
0x0053CA00 is called with an argument from 0x0053C900 but its body is void/argument-free; the extra argument is ignored under cdecl
tests_required: Parse a known-good .hdv and assert representative vehicle_physics offsets (0x40 mass, 0x13C4 forward gears) and car_setup offsets (0x1990 rules, 0x19A4 custom flag) hold expected values
Point hdv_file_path at a nonexistent path and assert 0x004F4270 returns -1 without partial struct writes
Set flags bit 0x2 and assert the damage-model/engine/gear FileFinder loads are skipped
Feed a malformed section and assert the illegal-file DebugLogWrite path fires without crashing
Load the same .mas twice via 0x0053CBC0 and assert the archive list (dword_8B8F14) does not corrupt and dword_8B6AC0 counts correctly; then remove via 0x0053CE40 and assert the count returns
